question: What was the loss ratio for each product in 2025?

sql:
WITH numerator AS (
    WITH source AS (
        SELECT c.*, p.channel, p.metro,
               coalesce(pay.paid, 0) AS paid_to_date,
               coalesce(pay.paid, 0) + c.reserve_amount AS incurred,
               c.close_date - c.report_date AS days_to_close
        FROM claims c
        JOIN policies p USING (policy_id)
        LEFT JOIN (
            SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) AS paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY claim_id
        ) pay USING (claim_id)
    )
    SELECT product, sum(incurred) AS value
    FROM source
    WHERE loss_date >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND loss_date <= DATE '2025-12-31'
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY ALL
),
denominator AS (
    WITH source AS (
        SELECT * FROM exposure_monthly
    )
    SELECT product, sum(earned_premium) AS value
    FROM source
    WHERE month >= DATE '2025-01-01'
      AND month <= DATE '2025-12-31'
    GROUP BY ALL
    ORDER BY ALL
)
SELECT product, 1 * numerator.value / nullif(denominator.value, 0) AS value
FROM numerator JOIN denominator USING (product)
ORDER BY ALL

input.sql: WITH pay AS (SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) paid FROM claim_payments GROUP BY 1), pay_d AS (SELECT claim_id, sum(amount) paid FROM (SELECT DISTINCT ON (claim_id, payment_date, amount, payee_type) * FROM claim_payments WHERE true ORDER BY claim_id, payment_date, amount, payee_type, load_batch) GROUP BY 1), inc AS (SELECT c.product, sum(coalesce(p.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount) raw, sum(coalesce(d.paid,0)+c.reserve_amount) dedup FROM claims c LEFT JOIN pay p USING(claim_id) LEFT JOIN pay_d d USING(claim_id) WHERE loss_date BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY 1), ep AS (SELECT product, sum(earned_premium) prem FROM exposure_monthly WHERE month BETWEEN '2025-01-01' AND '2025-12-31' GROUP BY 1) SELECT product, raw/prem AS loss_ratio_as_loaded, dedup/prem AS loss_ratio_deduplicated FROM inc JOIN ep USING(product) ORDER BY 1

report.interpretation: Loss ratio is incurred losses (paid plus reserve) divided by earned premium, using the agreed loss_ratio metric. I counted claims by loss date in calendar 2025 (1 Jan to 31 Dec) and split by product. The claims-data caveat on duplicate payments is below.
report.answer: For 2025, the home loss ratio was 61.3% and the motor loss ratio was 56.7%. Home ran about 4.6 percentage points higher. About 198 duplicated payment rows were reloaded in March 2026, so these figures are slightly overstated. With the duplicates removed, home would be about 60.5% and motor about 56.6%. Claims reported late and reserves still open on 2025 losses could also move these numbers.

findings.claim: 2025 loss ratio by product, as loaded: home 61.3%, motor 56.7%.

data_quality_issues.issue: claim_payments has 198 exact duplicate rows, all from the out-of-schedule load reload-2026-03-14 (payments dated 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-13).
data_quality_issues.impact: Paid amounts on some 2025-loss claims are overstated, which inflates the home loss ratio by about 0.8 points (to 61.3% from 60.5%) and the motor loss ratio by about 0.1 points. I did not adjust the headline figures. The adjusted values came from a separate deduplicating query.

data_quality_issues.issue: Late-reported claims and open reserves for 2025 losses may still develop.

proposed_actions.title: Remove duplicate rows from reload-2026-03-14 in claim_payments
proposed_actions.reason: 198 payment rows repeat existing payments and overstate paid and incurred amounts.

report.interpretation: This is the same loss ratio as before: incurred losses (paid plus reserve) divided by earned premium, with claims counted by loss date. "And for the first half of 2026" means losses dated 1 Jan to 30 Jun 2026, split by product, as a follow-up to the 2025 figures.
report.answer: For H1 2026, the home loss ratio was 63.1% and the motor loss ratio was 60.8%. Both are higher than in 2025 (home 61.3%, motor 56.7%), and motor rose more, by about 4.1 points against 1.8 for home. Two caveats apply. First, duplicated payments reloaded in March 2026 inflate these figures: with duplicates removed, home would be about 60.4% and motor about 57.3%. Most of the apparent rise is therefore the duplicates, and on the deduplicated basis motor is only slightly above 2025. Second, recent months are still incomplete because claims are reported late and reserves are still developing.
